title: The same electroceutical, monensin, induces tails at tail wounds and legs at leg wounds

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The same electroceutical, monensin, induces tails at tail wounds and legs at leg wounds

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Applied systemically, the same bioelectric-modifying drug (monensin) triggers tail regeneration at tail wounds and leg regeneration at leg wounds, showing that the specificity of the regenerative response lies in the responding cell collective rather than in the reagent.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Applications and a Roadmap Toward a Radical Regenerative Medicine › Top‐Down Control Exploits Agential Materials by Pushing Complexity from the Engineer onto the System Itself

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Even more remarkably, the exact same electroceutical—monensin—triggers tails in tail wounds and legs at leg wounds: the specificity in all of these cases is in the cell collective that responds to the stimulus [128, 200].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Applications and a Roadmap Toward a Radical Regenerative Medicine › Top‐Down Control Exploits Agential Materials by Pushing Complexity from the Engineer onto the System Itself”. Scope: Amphibian (Xenopus) tadpole tail and limb regeneration (author's lab's prior work, refs [128, 200])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Appendage identity is directly measurable and the contrasting response is strong. Existing reports can check each outcome, but raw data accessibility and cross-experiment comparability constrain the claim that the reagent is identical and specificity resides exclusively in the collective.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply matched systemic monensin exposure after tail and leg wounds and score regenerated structure identity, anatomy and function against vehicle controls. Site-appropriate appendages with no cross-identity outcomes support contextual specificity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The response location does not alone prove where specificity is encoded.

Systemic exposure at matched effective dose may not be demonstrated.

Tail and limb studies use different developmental stages and protocols.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Site-appropriate regeneration after one drug is a direct anatomical comparison, and tail experiments have published summary indices. The paired tail-versus-leg scores required by the claim are not in a public file, and the limb result has not been released as an analyzable replicate set. Checking specificity in the cell collective requires those data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Deliver the same systemic monensin treatment to animals with either a tail wound or a leg wound and score regenerate identity. Tails at tail wounds and legs at leg wounds would support specificity in the responding collective; identical structures at both sites, or no regeneration, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published tail regeneration indices are not a deposited animal-level dataset.

The froglet limb series is not available as public raw counts or an independent replication.

Systemic exposure has to be matched so that site differences are not dose differences.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data existence: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.35
